newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures end mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures end mostly lower.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures extended early losses to end mostly lower on Wednesday, reflecting the yen's rebound against the dollar later in the day, traders said.
Gold prices ranged from unchanged to six yen per gram lower. The most-active benchmark October contract finished five yen per gram weaker at 1,338 yen.
"The yen's rise invited long-liquidation by private investors in distant months, which overwhelmed sporadic fresh buying," a trading house trader said.
The gold market reacted little to overnight news of the International Monetary Fund's (IMF) proposed sale of five million ounces of gold.
In the bullion market, spot gold was a tad firmer at $378.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $377.85/378.25 in New York on Tuesday.
Spot gold was trapped within narrow ranges on Wednesday, sandwiched between producer selling above $378 and short-covering around $377 flat, the traders said.
"Sentiment will continue to be bearish as long as the U.S. stock market is firmer," one trader said.
